---
title: "How it works"
---

FileShare is a thin layer over the `tailscale` command line tool.

## Devices

The device list comes from `tailscale status --json`. A green dot means the device
is online. Taildrop only sends to devices logged in as you.

## Sending

Drop files on the window (or click the box to pick them). Each one goes out with:

```bash
tailscale file cp <file> <device>:
```

## Receiving

Every 5 seconds the window asks for new files, which runs:

```bash
tailscale file get --conflict=rename ~/Downloads/FileShare
```

Files with the same name are renamed, not overwritten.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Windows and macOS

The official Tailscale app may catch incoming files itself and put them straight
into your Downloads folder. So while FileShare is open, any file that newly appears
in Downloads is moved into `Downloads/FileShare`. It can't tell a Taildrop file from
a browser download, so both are moved. Files that were already there when FileShare
started are never touched.
:::

## Security

FileShare has no network listener of its own. The window talks to a tiny server
bound to `127.0.0.1` on a random port, protected by a random per-launch token, so
nothing outside your computer can use it.
